Since n < 10,000 and n is a positive integer, 2006 <= m < 12005. The number of factors d(m) = 21. The prime factorization of 21 is 3*7 or 21. Thus, m must be of the form p^20 or p^6 * q^2 for distinct primes p, q. 1) m = p^20: 2^20 > 12005, so no solutions. 2) m = p^6 * q^2: If p=2, m = 64*q^2. 2006 <= 64*q^2 < 12005 => 31.3 < q^2 < 187.5 => q \u2208 {7, 11, 13}. This gives m \u2208 {3136, 7744, 10816}, so n \u2208 {1131, 5739, 8811}. If p=3, m = 729*q^2. 2006 <= 729*q^2 < 12005 => 2.75 < q^2 < 16.4 => q = 2 (since q must be prime and distinct from p). This gives m = 729*4 = 2916, so n = 911. If p=5, m = 15625*q^2, which exceeds the range.
